title: Bipartite Graphs Are Not Well-Quasi-Ordered by Bipartite Minors: the tadpole is a bipartite minor but not a minor of the cycle (printed as Theorem 1)
author: Therese Biedl, Dinis Vitorino
work: Bipartite Graphs Are Not Well-Quasi-Ordered by Bipartite Minors
difficulty_reason: Counted unit: the article's Theorem 1 (source0.tex lines 271--274, source label thm: bip minor but not minor): the tadpole T(l,l_1) is a bipartite minor of the cycle C_p whenever p has the same parity as l and is at least l + 2 l_1, but is never a minor of any cycle. It is delivered with the article's complete original proof at source0.tex lines 276--300 (25 lines, one adjacent proof environment, no gap and no deferral). The proof is a genuine structural argument: it exhibits the explicit sequence of admissible contractions of the cycle that builds the tadpole with growing head and pole, verifying at each step that the contracted pair lies on a common cycle as the notion of an admissible contraction requires, and it then rules out the reverse minor relation through the maximum-degree invariant and the minor-closedness of the graphs of maximum degree at most two, a step that needs the observation that taking minors does not preserve maximum degree in general. The substantive content is the explicit contraction sequence and the invariant argument; neither is an unpacking of definitions. H2: a complete original research-paper theorem, moderately short, whose proof is a genuine combinatorial construction.

primary.theorem: Theorem 1 (thm: bip minor but not minor)
